title: Fossil Record and Rock Layer Evidence Review Test
description: Spaced review for interpret fossil placement, rock layers, and anatomical patterns to reason about life history over time.

questions.prompt: What is the usual age pattern in undisturbed rock layers?
questions.questionText: What is the usual age pattern in undisturbed rock layers?
options: lower layers are older than upper layers
all layers are the same age
age depends only on fossil size
questions.correctAnswer: lower layers are older than upper layers
questions.explanation: This is the basic relative-age rule.

questions.prompt: A fossil is below another fossil. What claim is best if layers are undisturbed?
questions.questionText: A fossil is below another fossil. What claim is best if layers are undisturbed?
options: The lower fossil is always alive.
The upper fossil must be fake.
Both fossils are the same object.
The lower fossil is probably older.
questions.correctAnswer: The lower fossil is probably older.

options: a colorful diagram with no labels
the same fossil sequence repeated in several rock formations
questions.correctAnswer: the same fossil sequence repeated in several rock formations

questions.prompt: Why check for folding or faults?
questions.questionText: Why check for folding or faults?
options: They turn fossils into living organisms.
They can disturb the original order of layers.
They prove all layers are young.
questions.correctAnswer: They can disturb the original order of layers.

questions.explanation: A trace fossil preserves evidence of activity.

questions.prompt: A table shows Trait X absent in old layers and common in young layers. What does that show?
questions.questionText: A table shows Trait X absent in old layers and common in young layers. What does that show?
options: proof the trait was chosen instantly
a pattern that may support change over time
questions.correctAnswer: a pattern that may support change over time
questions.explanation: Trait counts across layers can show trends.

questions.prompt: What is a careful fossil claim?
questions.questionText: What is a careful fossil claim?
options: The evidence supports this age relationship, but more samples could strengthen it.
questions.correctAnswer: The evidence supports this age relationship, but more samples could strengthen it.

questions.prompt: Why is the fossil record incomplete?
questions.questionText: Why is the fossil record incomplete?
options: Not every organism is preserved as a fossil.
No organisms lived in the past.
questions.correctAnswer: Not every organism is preserved as a fossil.

options: layer order -> fossil comparison -> evidence-based claim
questions.correctAnswer: layer order -> fossil comparison -> evidence-based claim

questions.prompt: A student says one fossil changed into the fossil above it. What is better?
questions.questionText: A student says one fossil changed into the fossil above it. What is better?
options: That is exactly how fossils work.
The upper fossil chose to evolve.
The fossils provide evidence about related forms or populations over time.
questions.correctAnswer: The fossils provide evidence about related forms or populations over time.
questions.explanation: Fossils are evidence, not living-changing individuals.

questions.prompt: Which data would support diversity change?
questions.questionText: Which data would support diversity change?
options: number of different fossil types in each layer
questions.correctAnswer: number of different fossil types in each layer

questions.prompt: What should scientists do with a faulted rock sequence?
questions.questionText: What should scientists do with a faulted rock sequence?
options: study how the fault moved layers before making an age claim
assume every top layer is oldest
questions.correctAnswer: study how the fault moved layers before making an age claim

options: This fossil pattern is evidence for a change, not a complete story by itself.
This one fossil proves the entire history of life.
All fossils form in the same year.
questions.correctAnswer: This fossil pattern is evidence for a change, not a complete story by itself.

questions.prompt: Why are hard shells often fossilized more than soft tissues?
questions.questionText: Why are hard shells often fossilized more than soft tissues?

questions.prompt: How can the fossil idea transfer to a new site?
questions.questionText: How can the fossil idea transfer to a new site?
options: Look for layer order, fossil patterns, and disturbance evidence before making claims.
questions.correctAnswer: Look for layer order, fossil patterns, and disturbance evidence before making claims.
questions.explanation: The same evidence rules apply in a new place.
